description: Given the head of a singly linked list and two integers left and right where left <= right, reverse the nodes of the list from position left to position right, and return the reversed list. Positions are 1-indexed.
intuition: Instead of actually removing and reinserting nodes, keep a pointer just before the reversal zone and repeatedly move the next node to the front of the reversed section. This 'thread-through' technique reverses the sublist in one pass without extra space.
approach: Navigate to the node just before position left. Then reverse the sublist from left to right by repeatedly moving the next node to the front of the reversed section.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5], left = 2, right = 4

dummy -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5
Advance prev to position 1 (node(1)):
  i=0: prev = node(1)

curr = node(2) (position "left")

Reverse right-left=2 times:

i=0: nextNode=node(3)
  curr.next = node(4)  [remove node(3)]
  nextNode.next = prev.next = node(2)
  prev.next = node(3)
  List: dummy->1->3->2->4->5, curr=node(2)

i=1: nextNode=node(4)
  curr.next = node(5)  [remove node(4)]
  nextNode.next = prev.next = node(3)
  prev.next = node(4)
  List: dummy->1->4->3->2->5

Return [1,4,3,2,5]
explanation:
1. Use a dummy node and advance prev to the node before position left.
2. curr starts at position left.
3. For each step, take the node after curr and move it to right after prev.
4. This effectively reverses the sublist one node at a time.
5. After (right - left) iterations, the sublist is fully reversed.
hints: Use a dummy node to handle the case where left = 1.
Find the node just before position left.
Reverse by repeatedly moving the next node to the front of the reversed section.

Create the dummy and return its next pointer

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Each move rewires a constant number of pointers. The suffix after right is never traversed.
